text:
Alex: Hey team — noticed a regression on the multi-GPU nightly after the kernel-selector change. 2x latency on long sequences, seems to correlate with KV cache churn and an NCCL all-reduce tail.
Maria: Ugh. Which job/run? link: https://perf.internal/runs/1890123
Alex: run id 2026-03-17-rt-8gpus. nsys capture attached: s3://redwood-profiles/1890123456.nsys
Joel: quick q — did the selector switch default quant kernels for head dims? That can change launch shapes and batching.
Alex: yes, we pick quantized_opt_v2 for z-head when seq_len>1024. change landed yesterday.
Anika: I grabbed a flame view. Timeline shows repeated short kernels alternating with NCCL hooks, allreduce invocations queueing up during KV prefetch windows.
perf-bot: perf summary: p99 latency went from 120ms -> 250ms; GPU util steady but %time in CUDA kernels jumped +18%. NCCL busy time increased +35%.
Maria: command I used for capture:
```
nsys profile --trace=cuda,nvtx,nccl --output out_1890123456 --sample=none --force true --capture-range=kernel --profile-child-processes true --wait=0 --capture-all-processes true --nvtx=true --stats=true --force-overwrite true --target-pid 4321
```
Joel: thanks. Any sign of kernel launch serialization? like many small kernels vs fewer big ones?
Anika: yes — kernel histogram shows a shift: avg kernel duration dropped from ~350us to ~40us, count up x8. That aligns with kernel splitting due to selector picking tile=32 path.
Alex: KV cache behavior: we see frequent cache invalidations during beam expansion, prefetcher is issuing async loads that overlap with collectives causing PCIe bursts. Trace shows repeated NVTX "kv:prefetch" spans overlapping NCCL:AllReduce calls.
Maria: Suggest trying two quick experiments: 1) force fallback to dense kernel path (tile=64) 2) throttle prefetcher concurrency to 2. Can we A/B?
Joel: I ran experiment 1 locally: forced kernel_selector.mode=dense and re-profiled — p99 dropped to 130ms, NCCL overlap reduced drastically. No correctness change.
Anika: experiment 2 (prefetch cap=2) also helped but less: p99 ~160ms. So both help; combined probably closer to baseline.
Alex: logs from nsys around the tail:
```
[...] nvtx:kv:prefetch begin 0x7f8e
kernel launch: launch_attention_kv_v2 grid=(256,1,1) block=(256,1,1) time=28us
nccl:AllReduce start (bytes=64MB)
kernel launch: tile_attention_dense grid=(64,1,1) time=420us
nvtx:kv:prefetch end 0x7f8e
nccl:AllReduce end
```
Maria: hypothesis: selector chooses fast small kernels to reduce single-token latency but increases kernel count and interleaves poorly with NCCL progress threads. Also prefetcher scheduling makes collectives wait for DMA bursts to finish (PCIe saturation).
Joel: possible fixes: - tweak kernel scoring to include downstream collective impact - add a batching heuristic to prefer fewer larger kernels when NCCL is active - make KV prefetch backoff if NCCL in-progress (use NVTX flags to detect)
Anika: note: on DGX-A100 topology, NVLink reduces PCIe pain, but our CI hardware is mixed (some PCIe-only), so regression shows up variably across clusters. Need guardrails.
Alex: action items: Maria -> open PR to add kernel_selector override flag and telemetry marker for kernel counts (due EOD). Joel -> prototype NCCL-aware kernel scoring (opt-in) and perf test. Anika -> add NVTX annotations to prefetcher and instrument DMA bytes in trace. I'll assemble a short reproducer job to run across both DGX and PCIe nodes.
Maria: +1. I'll also add a canary that forces fallback for customers on dedicated infra if p99 spikes after rollout.
perf-bot: Created perf ticket PERF-4829 and attached nsys file.
Joel: thanks. Small note — also check PyTorch version of NCCL: older NCCL can have slower progress when many small kernels are active. Might be an easier mitigation.
Alex: good call. I'll include that in the reproducibility matrix.
Anika: saving timeline snippets and kernel maps to s3://redwood-profiles/1890123456/extracted/
Alex: ok let's triage tomorrow morning 10am PT. @Maria @Joel @Anika please bring updated traces for the two experiments. :thumbsup:
